channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Egyptian journalist Lina Attalah faces prison as trial sparks international outcry
item.description: Egyptian journalist Lina Attalah, head of independent news outlet Mada Masr, faces a criminal court retrial Wednesday over charges of operating without a licence and publishing false news. The UN criticised Egypt’s “widening assaults on press freedom” Tuesday. Attalah was previously handed a one-year prison sentence in absentia in 2024.

item.title: Federal government failed to hold Epstein accountable, Republican committee says
item.description: The Republican chair of the House Oversight Committee released a scathing report after a 15-month investigation into Jeffrey Epstein and his associates. It faulted the federal government with decades of failing to hold Epstein accountable.

item.title: Boat capsized off Senegal's northwest coast leaving 39 dead
item.description: At least 39 people have died after a migrant boat capsized off Senegal, one of the country's deadliest migration tragedies in recent years. We'll try to understand why so many are still willing to put their lives at risk, with our guest Aissata Kane from the International Organization for Migration. Then, western Ethiopia is reeling after a deadly attack that left 65 people dead, including 27 civilians. As violence flares again near the Sudanese border, regional authorities are pointing the finger at neighbouring countries, accusing them of backing armed groups operating in the area. And, home fans have plenty to celebrate at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games. Two more taekwondo medals, including a gold, have propelled the host nation to sixth place in the standings.

item.title: Haiti PM praises Bukele after Salvadoran troops help destroy gang headquarters
item.description: Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aime praised Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele on Tuesday after Salvadoran troops destroyed a suspected gang leader’s home. Bukele’s deployment of more than 2,000 soldiers following four Salvadoran troops’ disappearance has raised concerns over rules of engagement and coordination with a UN-backed force combating Haiti’s gangs.

item.title: Missing 11-month-old boy taken by father found buried alive after 24 hours: Sheriff
item.description: The baby, Koah Sharpe, was found Tuesday afternoon "clinging to life," after spending what is believed to have been 24 hours buried, according to authorities.

item.title: WATCH: Video shows rescue of girl nearly swept away by wave in Oregon
item.description: As powerful waves hammer the Oregon coast, video shows the dramatic rescue of a child pulled into the surf by a so-called "sneaker" wave.

item.title: House tables Hegseth impeachment, effectively killing it in current Congress
item.description: Hegseth framed the effort as being directed at U.S. service members.

item.title: Kennedy family members ask a judge to block Trump's Arlington memorial arch
item.description: Nine Kennedy family members have asked a judge to block President Trump's plan to build a 250-foot memorial arch

item.title: Attempt to impeach Trump's defence secretary blocked
item.description: An attempt to impeach US defence secretary Pete Hegseth has been blocked following a vote in the House of Representatives on Tuesday.

item.title: House votes to effectively end the impeachment effort against Pete Hegseth
item.description: House Republicans managed to short-circuit a floor vote on the impeachment effort brought against the Defense Secretary by Kentucky Republican Thomas Massie.

item.title: Supreme Court seems split over federal agencies' ability to fine for law violations
item.description: The Supreme Court heard arguments Tuesday in a case related to temporary worker visas. The company involved says enforcement issues should go through the courts, not the federal agency alone.

item.title: Teddy Riner candidacy 'illustrative of this hunger for an alternative' to Le Pen or Mélenchon
item.description: As Teddy Riner throws his hat in the race for the French presidency, amid France's sociopolitical and economic crises. François Picard is pleased to welcome Lex Paulson, Director of Executive Programs at UM6P School of Collective Intelligence at at Mohammed VI Polytechnic University. The prospect of Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner entering France's presidential race raises questions that extend well beyond the political ambitions of a celebrated athlete. At a time when traditional parties are struggling to mobilize voters and the political center remains deeply fragmented, Riner's emergence points to a broader transformation in democratic competition: the growing importance of personal credibility, public visibility and the capacity to embody an alternative to established political elites. In an interview with France 24, Lex Paulson, Professor of Collective Intelligence at Mohammed VI Polytechnic University, argues that the changing relationship between voters and political instituti

item.title: Trump ally Jim Jordan elected House Republican leader after midterm defeat
item.description: Jim Jordan, a hardline ally of President Donald Trump, was elected US House Republican leader on Tuesday, defeating Steve Scalise 106-73 in a secret ballot, US media reported. He replaces Mike Johnson after Republicans lost both chambers of Congress in last week’s midterm elections and will lead the party’s opposition.

item.title: US charges three 'Iranian operatives' over RAF Fairford terror plot
item.description: The US Justice Department on Tuesday charged three men it described as Iranian operatives over an alleged September terrorist plot at Britain's RAF Fairford airbase in England. Prosecutors said one suspect directed individuals to drive vans, some carrying fuel barrels, to the base, which housed US military aircraft and personnel.

item.title: West Bank: Population and healthcare actors, such as MSF, 'still facing movement restrictions'
item.description: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Frederica Venturi of Doctors Without Borders (MSF). The withdrawal of Israeli forces from Hebron has not brought an end to the humanitarian crisis. According to Venturi, some 3,300 Palestinians were forcibly displaced, 15 houses were reportedly demolished, and continuing restrictions on movement have obstructed access to essential healthcare. "Those families whose houses were demolished have nowhere to go back to." Venturi describes how the "movement restrictions during the lockdown prevented medical teams from reaching communities." Hospitals are also reporting shortages of essential medicines.

item.title: Jimmy Carter's family farm to be preserved and opened to the public
item.description: The family farm where President Jimmy Carter tended peanuts, corn and sugarcane as a boy and returned throughout his life will be preserved and opened to the public

item.title: 'Europe not going anywhere': G7 summit a 'signal to Russians' that Europe is standing behind Ukraine
item.description: As the US Midterms reshape Ukraine diplomacy, Annette Young is pleased to welcome James Townsend, Atlantic Council's Senior Advisor at the Scowcroft Center's for Transatlantic Security Initiative. "Europe is not going anywhere." With this unequivocal assessment, Townsend, taking place alongside trilateral negotiations in Abu Dhabi. While the latter may command international attention, Townsend argues that the Paris meeting carries a message of its own: European support for Ukraine is intended to remain durable, and Moscow should not mistake diplomatic negotiations for an erosion of Western resolve. The G7 meeting therefore emerges as more than a forum for diplomatic declarations. It represents a test of Western cohesion, the credibility of future military and financial assistance, and Washington's willingness to endorse a common position on Ukraine. As Townsend emphasizes, the final communiqué will also be "a test as far as what Marco Rubio is going to agree to put his name to."

item.title: Eisenkot pushes October 7 inquiry as Netanyahu targets Arab parties in tense new parliament
item.description: Gadi Eisenkot, the politician tasked with forming a new Israeli government, pledged on Tuesday to launch an official inquiry into Hamas's October 7, 2023 attacks and reverse many of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's policies as the new parliament was sworn in a tense opening session that saw rival parties trade barbs over the possibility of forming a government with the support of Arab lists.

item.title: 'Central role in ecosystem: If something happens to Nvidia, it's going to be a catastrophe'
item.description: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Raphaëlle d’Ornano, Founder and Managing Partner of D’Ornano + Co. “Nvidia has an absolutely central role in the ecosystem,” she explains, “If something happens to Nvidia, it's going to be a catastrophe.” When the discussion turns to geopolitics, she warns, “there is a real war happening here. It's an economic war,” describing the competition for frontier AI capabilities as a struggle with profound economic, military, and societal implications. The resulting analysis reveals an industry characterized by extraordinary technological momentum, but increasingly shaped by concentrated corporate power, geopolitical confrontation, and political resistance to its physical infrastructure.

item.title: Anthropic eyes $1.4 trillion valuation in blockbuster IPO
item.description: US firm Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI chatbot, has announced it will offer 825 million shares at a price between $70 and $78 apiece during its planned IPO. This will give the firm a valuation of around 1.4 trillion dollars. The blockbuster IPO will come at a time investors are becoming increasingly concerned about risks associated with the AI boom. But first, chip giant Nvidia continues to face pressure over its CEO's love affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

item.title: Asymmetric cyberwarfare: 'States increasingly use cyberattacks in support of their other objectives'
item.description: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Rafe Pilling, Director of Threat Intelligence in the Sophos Counter Threat Unit (CTU). How can a minor cyber intrusion disrupt food supplies, expose the weaknesses of industrial infrastructure and become an instrument of geopolitical confrontation? The cyberattacks targeting supermarket refrigeration systems in France offer a revealing illustration of how digital vulnerabilities can translate into tangible economic disruption and potentially broader threats to society. As Pilling explains, “With a small amount of effort from the adversary side, they can create a large impact, in this case destroying food and producing empty shelves or empty refrigeration units in stores.” This asymmetry lies at the heart of contemporary cyber conflict, in which modest technical interventions can produce disproportionate economic and operational consequences

item.title: US soldier arrested in Britain on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence
item.description: UK police arrested a senior member of the US Army on Tuesday on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence, adding that the arrest was not related to other counter-terror investigations. The 41-year-old man was detained near the city of Gloucester, west England, and remains in custody.

item.title: What the hack? Europeans face growing psyops and cyberattacks
item.description: So this time, it's Iran, not Russia? France - reportedly acting on US intelligence - summoning Tehran’s ambassador over last month’s hacking of hundreds of supermarket refrigerators that overheated, 15 of which even caught fire. Why now at a time when Iran’s trying to break its international isolation?

item.title: Meghan's father sent to jail after 'cutting off' electronic tag
item.description: Thomas Markle has been sent to jail, accused of cutting off the electronic ankle tag monitoring his movements under house arrest.

item.title: House panel rebukes DOJ's handling of Epstein case
item.description: The House Oversight Committee, in a report summarizing its 15-month Jeffrey Epstein probe, rebuked the Justice Department's handling of the Epstein case.

item.title: Testing the new generation of AI-enabled fire-extinguishing drones
item.description: Drone makers are testing new, big drones that can deliver water or fire retardant with AI assistance. Aspen, Colorado is the first place trying them out. Cool and expensive? Yes. Effective? TBD.

item.title: U.S. boycotts U.N. human rights review for second year running
item.description: The U.S. has skipped a key U.N. human rights review for the second year running. Rights groups warn the absence risks undermining global accountability.

item.title: Senior US Army officer arrested in UK on allegations of Russia espionage
item.description: A senior US Army officer has been arrested in the UK over "allegations of espionage" related to Russia, according to British and American officials.

item.title: Ex-investigator admits depriving war crimes probe of potentially valuable information
item.description: A former senior investigating officer for the Royal Military Police has admitted depriving a war crimes investigation of potentially valuable information.

item.title: Filming amongst body bags: New Colombian president’s comms campaign sparks backlash
item.description: Since taking office in August, new far-right Colombian president Abelardo de la Espriella has shared video after video promoting his security forces – especially operations they’ve carried out against armed groups. In some, De la Espriella speaks standing among body bags. Others feature prisoners or look like they were taken from an action film. However, there’s been growing outcry about his social media glorification of repressive policies.

item.title: Train driver 'heard someone screaming' about knifeman stabbing people
item.description: The driver of a London-bound train on which 10 people were stabbed told a court he "heard someone screaming" through a door microphone that a knifeman was attacking people.

item.title: Americans across the economic spectrum feel a 'panic' about finances, author says
item.description: Mona Chalabi spent five years following Americans living paycheck to paycheck, as well as those earning top wages. Her new book, Ten Lives, explores why financial security can feel so elusive.

item.title: French police search Ritz, glitzy Al Fayed properties in women-trafficking probe
item.description: French police have searched several properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, in relation to an investigation into a suspected international network trafficking women for Mohamed Al Fayed, prosecutors told AFP on Tuesday. The Ritz is just one of the late tycoon's high-end ventures where victims have said they faced abuse.

item.title: Iran live updates: Hegseth says Trump 'kicked their teeth in'
item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.title: Sports legends whose political fortunes may be a lesson to Riner ahead of presidential bid
item.description: French judo star Teddy Riner may have announced his bid for the 2027 French presidential campaign on Monday, but he is not the only sports star to transition from stadium to bully pulpit. Read about some of his most famous predecessors.

item.title: Seven people taken to hospital after car collides with pedestrians
item.description: Seven people have been taken to hospital after a car collided with a "number of pedestrians" in Glasgow, police say.

item.title: Kristallnacht' 88th anniversary: Merz says Germany faces historic test over antisemitism
item.description: It has been 88 years since "Kristallnacht", the "Night of Broken Glass" in Europe, a violent pogrom against the Jewish population across Nazi Germany and Austria, marking a critical escalation toward the Holocaust. Friedrich Merz, Federal Chancellor of Germany, said that Germany currently faces a historic test over antisemitism.

item.title: US Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth calls impeachment moves 'a farce'
item.description: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday, November 10, called an effort to impeach him over ​abuse of power in the Iran war a farce and sabotage that plays into the hands of adversaries. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Commentator Douglas Herbert has more.

item.title: Who exactly is Pete Hegseth, the Pentagon chief facing an impeachment bid?
item.description: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday dismissed the impeachment effort against him as "a political spectacle". He made the comments a day after Republican Thomas Massie launched a bid to impeach him over his handling of the unpopular war in Iran and other actions. But who is Pete Hegseth? A former Fox News host and military veteran, he has become one of the most prominent figures in the Trump administration.

item.title: French students vow to keep up protest pressure for better learning conditions
item.description: France has been buffeted for months by street protests. They began in September ​with students ‌demanding the renovation of school buildings, more teachers and ⁠university reforms but then turned into broader cost-of-living protests, drawing in trade unions and political activists, and sometimes ‌turning violent.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV visits Argentina in second leg of Latin American tour
item.description: Pope Leo XIV visited Argentina on the second leg of his South American tour, following a stop in Uruguay. During his visit, he celebrated public Masses, met with the faithful and held talks with religious and government leaders. Peru is the final stop on the pontiff's tour.

item.title: REPLAY: US Secretary of State Rubio holds press conference after G7 meeting
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio talked to the press Tuesday as the G7 meets in Paris. He said he saw no need to resume major combat operations against Iran because economic restrictions were working so effectively. He also hailed US-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi as "very productive" and said the discussions should be expanded to include Europeans at the table.

item.title: French far right on track to secure €10 million loan for Le Pen's presidential campaign
item.description: France's far-right National Rally party on Tuesday reached a preliminary agreement with two European banks for a loan to help fund Marine Le Pen's presidential campaign. The lenders are expected to finalise the €10 million loan by the end of the month.

item.description: ABC News’ Chief Meteorologist Ginger Zee has some eye-opening demonstrations she hopes can help save lives during flash floods.

item.description: ‌Trinidad and Tobago's ‌law criminalising consensual sexual ​relations between male same-sex couples has been overturned ‌by a ​UK court.

item.description: Sophie has visited the Rohingya refugee camps at Cox's Bazar in Bangladesh to see the support being offered to displaced people from Myanmar.

item.description: Several people have contacted police with allegations and information about Russell Brand during his trial and after it concluded.

item.description: Gasoline prices fell below $4 a gallon Tuesday for the first time in three months — but the overall cost of living remains stubbornly high.

item.description: Little is known about her except that she's reportedly about 13 and named Kim Ju Ae, but Korea's spy agency says she's likely her father's heir.
